cases.expected_answer: An associate means a company, limited liability partnership or body corporate in which a director, trustee, partner, Sponsor or Manager of the Alternative Investment Fund, or a director or partner of the Manager or Sponsor, holds, individually or collectively, more than fifteen percent of its paid-up equity share capital or partnership interest.
cases.question: Under the SEBI AIF Regulations, what does 'associate' mean?

cases.expected_answer: A sponsor means any person or persons who set up the Alternative Investment Fund, and includes a promoter in case of a company and a designated partner in case of a limited liability partnership.
expected_key_facts: set up the Alternative Investment Fund
cases.question: Who is a 'sponsor' of an Alternative Investment Fund?

cases.expected_answer: Controlling interest means an interest, whether direct or indirect, to the extent of more than fifty percent of voting rights or interest.
cases.question: What does 'controlling interest' mean for the purpose of sub-clause (ii)?

cases.expected_answer: Social units means units issued by a social impact fund or schemes of a social impact fund to investors who have agreed to receive only social returns or benefits and no financial returns against their contribution.
cases.question: What are 'social units' under the regulations?

cases.expected_answer: An individual, Hindu Undivided Family, family trust or sole proprietorship needs annual income of at least two crore rupees; or net worth of at least seven crore fifty lakh rupees with at least three crores seventy-five lakh rupees in financial assets; or annual income of at least one crore rupees with minimum net worth of five crore rupees including at least two crore fifty lakh rupees in financial assets.
cases.question: What income and net-worth thresholds must an individual meet to be an accredited investor?

cases.expected_answer: An existing fund falling within the AIF definition but not registered may continue for six months from commencement, or till disposal of its registration application if applied within six months; the Board may extend this up to twelve months in special cases. Existing schemes complete their agreed tenure but raise no fresh monies till registration.
cases.question: How long may an existing unregistered fund continue to operate after commencement of the regulations?

cases.expected_answer: A Category I Alternative Investment Fund invests in start-up or early stage ventures, social ventures, SMEs, infrastructure or other sectors the government or regulators consider socially or economically desirable, including venture capital funds, SME funds, angel funds, social impact funds, infrastructure funds and special situation funds.
cases.question: What is a Category I Alternative Investment Fund?

cases.expected_answer: The applicant, Sponsor and Manager must be fit and proper persons under Schedule II of the Intermediaries Regulations, 2008. The Manager's key investment team must include at least one key personnel with relevant Board-specified certification and at least one with professional qualification in finance, accountancy, business management, commerce, economics, capital market or banking, or a CFA charter.
cases.question: What fit-and-proper and key-team conditions apply for AIF registration?

cases.expected_answer: No. An Alternative Investment Fund granted registration under a particular category cannot change its category subsequent to registration, except with the approval of the Board.
cases.question: Can an AIF change its category after registration?

cases.expected_answer: If the Board opines that a certificate should not be granted, it may reject the application after giving the applicant a reasonable opportunity of being heard. The rejection must be communicated within thirty days, and the applicant must cease any AIF activity, without affecting liability to existing investors.
cases.question: What is the procedure when the Board refuses AIF registration?

cases.expected_answer: Any material alteration to the fund strategy requires the consent of at least two-thirds of unit holders by value of their investment in the Alternative Investment Fund.
cases.question: What consent is needed for a material alteration to fund strategy?

cases.expected_answer: The Manager or Sponsor must maintain a continuing interest of not less than two and a half percent of the corpus or five crore rupees, whichever is lower, as investment (not through waiver of management fees). For Category III the interest must be not less than five percent of the corpus or ten crore rupees, whichever is lower. No scheme shall have more than one thousand investors.
cases.question: What continuing interest must the Manager or Sponsor maintain in the fund?

cases.expected_answer: Extension of a close-ended scheme's tenure may be permitted up to two years with approval of two-thirds of unit holders by value; an Accredited Investors only fund may extend up to five years with such approval.
cases.question: By how much may the tenure of a close-ended scheme be extended?

cases.expected_answer: Units of a close-ended Alternative Investment Fund may be listed on a stock exchange subject to a minimum tradable lot of one crore rupees, and listing is permitted only after final close of the fund or scheme.
cases.question: When may units of a close-ended AIF be listed on a stock exchange?

cases.expected_answer: Category III Alternative Investment Funds shall invest not more than ten per cent of the investable funds in an investee company, directly or through other AIF units; large value funds for accredited investors of Category III may invest up to twenty per cent. For listed equity the ten (or twenty) per cent limit may alternatively be computed on the net asset value of the scheme.
cases.question: What is the single-company investment limit for Category III AIFs?

cases.expected_answer: No. Category I Alternative Investment Funds shall not borrow funds directly or indirectly or engage in any leverage for making investments or otherwise, except borrowing to meet temporary funding requirements; they may engage in hedging, including credit default swaps, as specified by the Board.
cases.question: Can Category I AIFs borrow funds or use leverage?

cases.expected_answer: Such investment shall be locked in for a period of one year from the date of investment.
expected_key_facts: one year from the date of investment
cases.question: What lock-in applies to investments under the SME-exchange exemption?

cases.expected_answer: At least seventy-five percent of the investable funds must be invested in unlisted securities or partnership interest of social ventures (or related units/securities). Grants are allowed only for that purpose, with a minimum grant of ten lakh rupees per person; the minimum does not apply to accredited investors.
cases.question: What deployment and grant rules apply to social impact funds?

cases.expected_answer: Category II Alternative Investment Funds shall not borrow or use leverage for investment purposes, except borrowing to meet temporary funding requirements and day-to-day operational requirements for not more than thirty days.
cases.question: What borrowing is permitted to Category II AIFs?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. Category III Alternative Investment Funds may engage in leverage or borrow subject to consent from the investors and a Board-specified maximum limit, with periodic disclosure of the overall leverage level, cash-borrowing leverage, derivatives/complex-product leverage and the main leverage source.
cases.question: Can Category III AIFs use leverage, and under what conditions?

cases.expected_answer: Angel funds shall raise funds only from accredited investors by issue of units (key management personnel of the fund or manager may also invest). No minimum investment value applies to angel investors, and funds are raised through private placement via information or placement memorandum.
cases.question: From whom may angel funds raise money, and is there a minimum investment?

cases.expected_answer: An angel fund must on-board at least five accredited investors before declaring its first close (otherwise it must refile the placement memorandum with the requisite fee). An angel fund shall not launch any schemes for soliciting funds or making investments.
cases.question: How many accredited investors must an angel fund on-board before first close, and may it launch schemes?

cases.expected_answer: Angel funds shall not invest in associates. Each investment in an investee company must have contribution from at least two accredited investors, and no contribution may come from angel investors who are a related party to the investee company.
cases.question: What associate and contribution restrictions apply to angel fund investments?

cases.expected_answer: Neither. An angel fund shall not launch any schemes for soliciting funds or making investments, and units of angel funds shall not be listed on any recognised stock exchange.
cases.notes: multi-chunk: scheme bar plus listing bar
cases.question: Can an angel fund launch schemes to solicit funds, and can its units be listed on a stock exchange?

cases.expected_answer: Special situation funds shall invest only in special situation assets and may act as resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. They shall not invest in associates, in units of other AIFs (other than special situation funds), or in special situation funds managed or sponsored by their own manager, sponsor or associates.
cases.question: What may special situation funds invest in, and what is prohibited?

cases.expected_answer: The Corporate Debt Market Development Fund is constituted as a Trust by registered deed and is a close-ended fund with a tenure of fifteen years from the date of its first closing; it must apply for AIF registration under Chapter II.
cases.question: What is the tenure and form of the Corporate Debt Market Development Fund?

cases.expected_answer: Extension of a migrated venture capital fund's tenure may be permitted up to two years with approval of two-thirds of unit holders by value; absent consent or after the extended tenure, the fund or scheme is wound up under Regulation 29 (except sub-regulation 9A).
cases.question: What tenure extension is permitted for a migrated venture capital fund?

cases.expected_answer: The Sponsor or Manager must appoint a Board-registered custodian for safekeeping of securities when the corpus exceeds five hundred crore rupees; a Category III AIF must appoint such a custodian irrespective of corpus size.
cases.question: When must an AIF appoint a custodian for safekeeping of securities?

cases.expected_answer: Records including the rationale for investments must be maintained for five years after winding up. A trust-structured AIF is wound up when the tenure of the fund or all its schemes ends, when the trustees opine winding up is in investors' interests, or when seventy-five percent of investors by value resolve so.
cases.question: How long must an AIF maintain records, and when is a trust-structured AIF wound up?

cases.expected_answer: The registration fee for angel funds is two lakh rupees (Rs. 2,00,000); refiling an angel fund placement memorandum costs one lakh rupees (Rs. 1,00,000); the Corporate Debt Market Development Fund registration fee is five lakh rupees (Rs. 5,00,000).
cases.question: What is the registration fee for angel funds and for refiling their placement memorandum?
What is the procedure for obtaining a driving licence in India?
What are the current contribution rates for the Employees' Provident Fund?
